title: Proportional-fairness admission controller for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a proportional-fairness admission controller for Dedicated capacity to enforce throughput guarantees while maximizing overall cluster utilization. This ticket covers design, implementation, and canary rollout for: (1) a weighted rate-limiter that allocates request tokens to customers/tenants proportionally to their reserved throughput and recent usage; (2) an adaptive queueing layer that enforces per-tenant queue depth and global queue headroom tied to autoscaler signals; (3) graceful overload shedding that applies progressively: request slowing, batching coalescing, reactive model downgrade, and finally request rejection with informative error payloads. Goal: keep tail latency within SLOs for committed tenants while preserving best-effort throughput for leftover capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Weighted rate limiter enforces reserved throughput within +/-5% under steady-state synthetic load tests
Queueing policy prevents queue depth from exceeding configured headroom under autoscaler cold-start scenarios in 95% of runs
Overload shedding flow triggers in documented order (slowdown -> batch -> downgrade -> reject) and provides consistent error/telemetry payloads
Canary rollout on internal Dedicated pool shows no P90 latency regression >10% for reserved customers over 24h
Integration tests added for fairness index (Jain) and shed rate metrics; PR merged and e2e passes in CI
design_decisions: Use token-bucket per-customer with dynamic weight adjustments based on (reserved_throughput * reservation_weight) + recent_consumption_factor
Proportional fairness: when capacity constrained, reduce each customer's effective rate by a factor that equalizes (allocated/reserved) ratios rather than strict priority preemption

Queueing model: two-tier queues — fast-path short queue for low-latency requests and spillover queue for batched/large requests. Queue headroom is a function of autoscaler predicted ramp and current available GPUs
Autoscaler integration: expose headroom_estimate signal from autoscaler; controller reduces admission aggressiveness when headroom < threshold

Shedding policy: ordered steps with timers and counters; first increase request processing delay (soft backpressure), then coalesce small requests into batch windows, then switch to lower-precision model variant (if available), finally return structured 429 with suggested retry-after and explanation
Telemetry: track allocated_rate, reserved_rate, actual_consumption, queue_time, shed_count, downgrade_count, fairness_index (Jain). These inform both autoscaler and product dashboards
Operational control: implement kill-switch and tiered feature flags (global, per-fleet, per-tenant) to quickly disable new behavior if regressions appear
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype token-bucket + weight adjustment in runtime simulator. Validate fairness under synthetic mixed workloads. Reference: confluence.redwood.internal/dedicated/admission/proportional-fairness (draft)
Phase 2: Implement admission controller in serving-runtime sidecar; lightweight path so main inference loop remains unchanged. Add metrics and tracing hooks.
Phase 3: Hook into autoscaler to consume headroom_estimate and to emit feedback metrics. Implement queue headroom controller that can be tuned via config flags.
Phase 4: Implement soft-shed steps (delay -> batch -> downgrade -> reject). Add clear structured error schema and SDK guidance for clients.
Phase 5: Add e2e tests and chaos experiments (simulate cold autoscaler scaling, partial zone outage) to validate graceful degradation.
Phase 6: Canary rollout to a small internal Dedicated pool, collect 48h of telemetry, iterate, then wider rollout to customers with opt-in beta
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged release: default off for customer fleets; enable on internal fleets first
Canary group: 3 internal Dedicated pools representing small, medium, large workload mixes for 72h
Metrics gating: only progress to next stage if P90 latency for reserved tenants does not increase by >10% and shed_rate < 0.5%
Beta opt-in customers: invite 5 paying customers with dedicated contracts and SLAs; commit to 2-week monitoring window and immediate rollback option
Full rollout: staged over weeks with automated canary checks and a manual approval gate handled by SRE on-call
metrics_to_monitor: shed_rate and breakdown by soft/medium/hard steps
downgrade_count (model falls back to smaller/quantized variants)
error rate (429 + custom structured errors) and client retry behavior
cost delta (tokens/GPU) under mixed load compared to baseline
comments: 2025-03-01 - Aisha Khan: Created initial ticket. Rationale: customers with reserved capacity are seeing intermittent tail-latency regressions during traffic spikes when autoscaler cold-starts. Existing priority-based shedders are too punitive to best-effort tenants and waste leftover headroom.

2025-03-03 - Marco Diaz: Added prototype notes — ran a simulator with 50 tenants; proportional fairness kept Jain index >0.9 and improved overall GPU utilization by ~8%. Attached preliminary charts to Confluence.

2025-03-05 - Priya Sharma (SRE): Review feedback — please add explicit circuit-breaker thresholds for zone failures and ensure downgrade path logs redaction for customer PII. Suggest adding a kill-switch that disables downgrades but preserves delay/batching.

2025-03-07 - Marco Diaz: Implemented basic weight-adjusted token bucket in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2318. Unit tests added. Integration test harness updated to simulate autoscaler headroom. PR link in attachments.

2025-03-10 - Aisha Khan: Meeting notes — agreed on telemetry schema and metric names. Decided to expose per-tenant suggested_retry_after in structured error so SDKs can surface guidance. Security review required for downgrade model variants (KMS keys and audit).
